clues: This city began as a small village on the east bank of a creek. Wild salt marshes spread around it on the flat plains.
No sea or high land sits near to soften the weather here. So winters bite with hard cold, and summers hit with waves of heat.
In 1867, a state team toured new sites for the capital, far from the old seat. They picked this tiny salt marsh village to take the job.
This town took a new name for President Abraham, who had just been shot dead. Some hoped that name would stop the move here, but it did not work.
The governor of Nebraska works in this city. All the state lawmakers meet here to make laws.
